title: Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN)

terms.operative: Literal or expression binding inside a dataInputAssociation passing an argument to a callActivity or globalTask.
Reusable sub-process invocation referencing another diagram by QName.
Collaboration diagram container binding participants and message flows.
Declared input parameter of a process, callActivity, or globalTask ioSpecification.
Binding that supplies an input parameter or dataStoreReference to an activity or callActivity.
Reference listing a declared dataInput inside an ioSpecification inputSet.
Binding that records an activity writing to a dataStoreReference (such as work-plan, log, or session-record).
Shared persistent store declared in global-tasks.bpmn (work-plan, corpus, log, session-record) and paired with a store Role.
Process-local reference to a shared bpmn:dataStore read or written by activities in the diagram.
Root element of a BPMN diagram carrying namespaces and targetNamespace.
Authored prose description attached to a process, lane, or activity.
Terminal node marking completion of a process execution path.
Conditional XOR decision branching or converging control flow.
Extension container holding role bindings, skills, and preconditions.
Reference connecting a process activity or gateway into a specific lane.
Source expression or literal inside a bpmn:assignment.
Reusable script-executed task definition in global-tasks.bpmn invoked by callActivity nodes across processes.
Reusable callable task definition in global-tasks.bpmn invoked by callActivity nodes across processes.
External vocabulary or schema import declaration on a BPMN definitions root.
Incoming sequence flow connection entering an activity or gateway.
Parameter set grouping the dataInputRefs required by an ioSpecification.
Input/output signature declaring the dataInput, inputSet, and outputSet of a process, callActivity, or globalTask.
Process swimlane establishing the role persona responsible for activities.
Container partitioning a process into one or more participant swimlanes.
Loop marker on an activity indicating parallel or sequential execution across a collection (such as target locales).
Outgoing sequence flow connection leaving an activity or gateway.
Output parameter set declared inside an ioSpecification.
Concurrent AND fork or join synchronization of parallel execution paths.
Swimlane participant representing a collaboration role or system boundary.
Top-level executable workflow definition containing activity flow nodes.
Top-level actor or system resource declaration referenced by process lanes.
Directed transition connecting source and target flow nodes.
Automated system task invoked during workflow execution.
Source element reference inside a dataInputAssociation (or sequenceFlow attribute in MODEL#).
Entry node initiating execution of a workflow process.
Target dataInput or dataStoreReference inside a dataInputAssociation or dataOutputAssociation (or sequenceFlow attribute in MODEL#).
Base unit of atomic work within a business process flow.
Timer schedule trigger defining timeouts or delayed transitions.
Target parameter expression inside a bpmn:assignment.
Interactive step requiring explicit human or agent persona execution.

note:
The `20100524` in every namespace is BPMN 2.0's release date and is how the edition is identified in an instance document — the diagrams have carried it since the first one was drawn, and until 2026-09-20 nothing in this repository said which specification that was. `conforms` rather than `reads`: these are our instance documents, so a version bump is a migration of the corpus rather than a compatibility question.

No XSD is held and none is fetched — referenced, per the owner's "dont need to materalize, but should reference specific version being used". That means nothing validates a diagram structurally against OMG's schema; `check:workflows` and `kg:audit` check the things this repository cares about (lanes bind declared roles, activities name skills) and are not a substitute for it.

The `MODEL#` form is the RDF spelling of the same namespace: OMG publishes no RDF vocabulary for BPMN, so a graph that states a sequence flow's `sourceRef`/`targetRef` or a node's `incoming`/`outgoing` (kg-export, and bootstrap-tools' `export-graph.ts`) names BPMN's own attribute by appending `#` to its XML namespace — the model's name for the relation, rather than a second one minted here (owner, 2026-09-30, bean `xsqm`).
